notes.title: Possible Connection Issues After October 1, 2025
notes.notes:
[p]Greetings, Brinehunters![/p][p][/p][p]We’ve recently been informed of an upcoming change from [b]Epic Online Services (EOS)[/b], the platform that powers our online features. Starting [b]October 1, 2025[/b], some [b]Windows players[/b] using older EOS versions (including the one currently used by Abyssus) [i]may[/i] experience connection issues.[/p][p][/p][p]What does this mean for you?[/p][p][/p][list][*][p]If your Windows system is [b]fully updated[/b], you should be fine.[/p][/*][*][p]If you encounter errors, you can fix them by either: [/p][olist][*][p]Installing the latest Windows Updates (recommended).[/p][/*][*][p]Manually installing the new security certificate (see below for the full runthrough).[/p][/*][/olist][/*][/list][p][/p][p]We’re already working on updating Abyssus to the latest EOS SDK. This will ensure long-term stability and prevent these issues altogether.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p]

[b]Manual Certificate Installation (Windows)[/b][/p][p][/p][p]If you experience connection issues after [b]October 1, 2025[/b] and updating Windows doesn’t solve it, you can manually install the required security certificate by following these steps:[/p][olist][*][p][b]Open the Start menu[/b] → type cmd.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Right-click on "Command Prompt"[/b] and select [b]"Run as Administrator"[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Copy and paste the following command into the window, then press [b]Enter[/b]:[/p][/*][/olist][p]curl [url="https://account-public-service-prod03.ol.epicgames.com/account/"]https://account-public-service-prod03.ol.epicgames.com/account/[/url][/p][p]     4. Once the process completes, restart your computer.[/p][p]     5. Relaunch Abyssus and try connecting again.[/p][p][/p][p]⚠️ [b]Note[/b]: This method is only needed if Windows Updates are not applied or do not work. The easiest and safest solution remains updating Windows regularly.[/p][p]

- The DoubleMoose Team[/p][p]

notes.title: Roadmap Blog
notes.notes:
[p]Greetings, Brinehunters!

Thank you for being with us during the launch of Abyssus. We’re very happy to see so many of you enjoying the game! [/p][p][/p][p]We want to reiterate our post-launch plans:

We have a lot of post-launch content planned, and all of it will be [b]free[/b].[/p][p][/p][p]We will never sell new content such as new weapons, abilities, game modes, etc. The only DLCs that will be paid for are supporter packs that add cosmetics and emotes. People can buy these if they want to support us as a studio, but it will never be required to get the latest, coolest stuff we’ve added to the game. [/p][p][/p][p]Here’s a brief preview of the updates we’re working on:
[/p][list][*][p][b]Infinite Mode[/b]: lets you continue playing indefinitely until you feel ready to face the final boss, with enemies infinitely scaling. We are excited to see who can make the most broken build and reach the furthest depths![/p][/*][*][p][b]Random Order Mode[/b]: keeps things fresh by switching up the areas so they’re not always in the same order. If you play with Random Order Mode on, you might start in Area 3, then go to Area 1, and so on. It will take some balance work to get it right, but we think this will be appreciated by those who play the game the most.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Alternative boss patterns[/b]: new movesets for the bosses, so you never really know which ones you’ll get in your next expedition.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Of course, we’ll also be adding new weapons, weapon mods, abilities, and some more secret stuff we want to keep as a surprise. [/p][p][/p][p]After the 1.1 and 1.2 patches, we will take a step back, listen to community feedback, and figure out what our next updates should be.[/p][p]
We don’t want to reveal everything right now, but we want our players to know that we intend to keep updating Abyssus according to your feedback and to what we think will make the best game in the long run. 

We love this game, and we love working on it. So, if you have any suggestions, feedback, or ideas, please leave a comment below![/p][p][/p][p]We also just released a new hotfix. notes.title: Abyssus system requirements
notes.notes:
As a long-time Deep Rock Galactic veteran, I'm not surprised to see that the Abyssus system requirements demand very little of your gaming laptop or PC. Both games offer procedurally-generated roguelite experiences and a four-player co-op experience, but Abyssus brings an underwater twist and some Hades-style elements I can't wait to get stuck into.

Abyssus could well become one of the best co-op games on PC and dominate the next few weeks of my life if the full release lives up to the demo and the gameplay trailers. The combat has a very Doom-like vibe, but with all the customization options I came to love in Deep Rock Galactic. However, time will tell if Abyssus can rise to the surface among a sea of other co-op roguelites, or sink to the abyss in obscurity, especially as you'll need a fairly decent if not the best gaming CPU you can afford from our buying guides to play the game at its best.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Abyssus (PC) Review
notes.notes:
Abyssus answers the question of what a game like Hades would feel like if it were a fast and frenetic boomer shooter with friends, set in a retro science fiction pulp setting ripped out of the 1960s.

Up to four players take on the mantle of brine hunters, intrepid explorers of the depths of the abyss. Despite not really caring about the overall narrative or hidden story beats peppered throughout the game world, one thing Abyssus does nail as far as its narrative is the voices of the playable characters. If you’re a fan of games like Deep Rock Galactic, you’ll feel right at home with the humorous, nonchalant attitude of the brine hunters despite the ever-increasing dangers that lurk down below.

Set across 64 levels punctuated by four distinct biomes, Abyssus is an addictive rougelike that is hard to put down. In other words, DoubleMoose Games has nailed the roguelike formula in delivering their debut title.

notes.title: Price Announcement and Plans for the Future
notes.notes:
[p]Greetings, Brinehunters![/p][p] [/p][p]In but a few days, you'll be diving into the Abyss for brine, gold, and glory, and we want to update you on the price of Abyssus, along with a few extra goodies and a very important statement about what to expect from Abyssus in the future.[/p][p]
[/p][p]First things first: [b]Abyssus will be priced at 24,99 USD/EUR[/b]. 
Remember that the price varies from region to region. 

Moreover, to celebrate the launch of Abyssus, we'll be having a [b]15% discount running during the launch week![/b] [/p][p]
Furthermore, we want to make our commitments for Abyssus' post-launch crystal clear: [/p][p]
[/p][p][b]ALL GAME CONTENT UPDATES WILL BE FREE.
[/b] [/p][p]For those interested in supporting our work, we will be offering optional cosmetics, emote packs, and goodies that won’t affect the game’s content.[/p][p]
[/p][p]We already have two major free content post-launch updates in the works, which we will be showing soon in our upcoming roadmap. We plan to include new game modes, weapons, mods, and other ideas, both from our studio and from community feedback. We want this content to enhance the Abyssus experience without an additional price tag. [/p][p]
We want these free updates to let you revisit the underwater ruins of Abyssus and explore the new features of each content patch without spending more money. [/p][p]
We want future players to have access to the same content as Day-1 players without having to cough up more money on DLCs to put their gaming experience on par.

If you like this philosophy and want to support us in making Abyssus better over time, buying the cosmetic packs is a great way to support our post-launch efforts without affecting the game's features.

[/p][p]Speaking of which, here are the first two additional goodies to start your descent into the depths in style![/p][p]
[/p][p]The first is a [b]digital edition of the game's OST[/b], composed by Remi Gallego AKA The Algorithm, and mixed by the great guys at Kid Katana Records! [/p][p]
[/p][p]Then we have our very own [b]Brinehunter Pack[/b], containing an exclusive helmet, a portrait frame, and a dance emote![/p][p]
[/p][p]Priced respectively at [b]4,99 USD/EUR[/b] and[b] 2,99 USD/EUR[/b], those are the first "something more" we wanted to offer you. And if you choose to support us at launch by buying the game and the goodies, we have prepared [b]two bundles, discounted by 10%[/b] on top of the one-week 15% launch discount on the game!

[/p][p]In the meantime, check your diving suit, tighten those straps, and load up some ludicrous firepower -[b] the expedition starts on August 12![/b][/p][p]
[/p][p]- The team at DoubleMoose Games.

notes.title: How to carry over your Demo saves to the full game
notes.notes:
[p]Greetings, Brinehunters![/p][p]
[/p][p]As we have stated, you will be able to carry over your saved game from the demo to the full version of Abyssus. And yet, to do so effectively, there is a simple manipulation to perform. Nothing like standing on a beacon to charge it while shots are being fired all around you![/p][p][/p][p]What you need to do:[/p][p][/p][p]1) Find the folder located at:[/p][p][b]C:\\Users\\Username\\AppData\\Local\\AbyssusDemo\\Saved\\SaveGames[/b]
[/p][p]2) Find the file called [b]SAVE_GAME_SESSION_SLOT.sav[/b] and the file called [b]\[your username].sav [/b]
[/p][p]3) Move both files into the folder located at:[/p][p][b]C:\\Users\\Username\\AppData\\Local\\Abyssus\\Saved\\SaveGames[/b][/p][p]
That's it! Once you start the full version of Abyssus, the demo save will be carried over to the full game. To prevent accidental savefile deletion during demo uninstall, [b][u]we are delaying the demo retirement until launch day, allowing players who wish to safeguard their files to do so.
[/u][/b]

notes.title: ABYSSUS LAUNCHES AUGUST 12 – NEW STEAM NEXT FEST DEMO IS LIVE!
notes.notes:
Listen up, Brinehunters!

We know you’ve been itching for adventure, and our first demo wasn’t enough to fill your cravings for iron, steam, and brine. We heard you, and we’re thrilled to reveal that you’ll be able to plunge into the full depths of the Abyss on [b][u]August 12, 2025[/u][/b]!

But be careful. In the deepest fathoms of the sea, now one will hear you scream – so you’d better prepare for your expedition. 
Lucky for you, we’ve cooked you the perfect training program.

[h3]Discover what awaits you in our Release Date Trailer:[/h3]
[previewyoutube=vnAWfATPH3I;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]A New Demo Surfaces![/h3]
To be sure you’re prepared for your upcoming dive on August 12, we’ve come up with a brand-new expedition:
Dive into the all-new [b]Gardens[/b] biome, a lush yet haunting domain where aquatic guardians stand ready to defend the ruins of their lost civilization from intruders.

And since the challenges will be tougher than before, we’ve got you covered with a [b]brand-new, electrifying weapon[/b]: the [b][u]Tesla rifle[/u][/b]! Its electric power can be concentrated onto a target or arc among the enemies, delivering devastating bursts of damage to tightly packed enemies. Its true potential is unleashed through secondary mods, enabling powerful charged attacks. 

The Tesla Gun will be joining the arsenal you’re already familiar with:

notes.title: ABYSSUS ALPHA OPENS TOMORROW!
notes.notes:
Gather your friends and dive into the unknown with [b][i]Abyssus,[/i][/b] a wild and exciting [b]“Brinepunk” Roguelike FPS[/b] that drops you right into the depths of an ancient underwater city.
Get ready for [b]non-stop action, tons of customization[/b], and a one-of-a-kind [b]underwater adventure![/b]

[h3]Discover the Announcement Trailer:[/h3] 
[previewyoutube=Nde1ob2AqqQ;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Explore the Abyss. Master its Power. Survive its Depths.[/h3]
In a world powered by brine –a rare and powerful substance only found in the deepest fathoms of the sea, your team of mercenary explorers is recruited to retrieve a massive deposit located beneath the ruins of a long-lost civilization. Nice and easy, right? It would be, if it weren't for the corrupted, bloodthirsty inhabitants lurking within this sunken kingdom. 

Team up with fellow [b]Brinehunters,[/b] uncover the ocean's forgotten secrets, and blast your way through hordes of corrupted enemies!💥

🌊 Will you survive to see the surface again, or will the Abyss claim your life?

[h3]Gear Up. Wield Godly Powers. Go Deeper Into the Abyss. Die. Repeat.[/h3]
Your best chance to survive in Abyssus is by mastering the ocean of weapon and character customization. Run after run, unlock new gear, and carefully choose synergic loadouts, skills, suits, and weapon mods to progress deeper into the Abyss.

And, who knows? You and your team of Brinehunters might be fortunate enough to receive blessings from divine forces…

[h3]The Abyss is Waiting for You[/h3]
Wanna take a dive and face the Abyss? We've got you covered! 
We're launching an [b]Alpha,[/b] which you can [b]join anytime while it's live by clicking on the opt-in button on the game's store page![/b]

[u][b]Check out the dates:[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Friday, December 6 (3PM CET) - Monday, December 9 (3PM CET)
[*] Friday, December 13 (3PM CET) - Monday, December 16 (3PM CET)
[*] Friday, December 20 (3PM CET) - Monday, December 23 (3PM CET)
[/list]

[h3]Important note on progression[/h3]
Your progression won't be wiped during these playtest sessions. You’ll be able to come back, pick up right where you left off, and continue to explore the Abyss throughout the Alpha phases.

[h3]Dive into the Alpha:[/h3]
Wondering what awaits you at the bottom of the ocean? Well, be ready for:
[list]
[*] [b]Solo or Co-op Experience:[/b] Dive into the depths solo or team up with up to three of your buddies!
[*] [b]Luxuriant and mysterious ruins:[/b] Explore and survive in two areas swarmed by corrupted ennemies
[*] [b]Two Boss Battles and Miniboss Fights:[/b] Challenge yourself against some tough opponents.
[*] [b]Powerful Blessings and Weapon Mods:[/b] Try out different skills and gear to discover what playstyle suits you best.
[/list]
[h3]What feedback are we looking for?[/h3]
We're launching an Alpha to ensure Abyssus will deliver the best possible experience. This early test phase aims at stress-testing our servers and gathering valuable feedback about the game's features, mechanics, and overall gameplay.
To make your feedback as impactful as possible, please let us know what you think about:
[list]
[*] [b]Progression[/b]: Do upgrades feel impactful?
[*] [b]Difficulty[/b]: Is the challenge level enjoyable? Well paced?
[*] [b]Weapons[/b]: What do you think about the balance? The gunfeel?
[*] [b]Abilities[/b]: Which one did you prefer? Why?
[*] [b]Gods[/b]: Again, which one did you prefer, and why? What do you think about the synergies? Do you have favorites?
[*] [b]UI & UX[/b]: Does the interface feel intuitive? Is it easy to understand and read? Could some mechanics be explained better? [/list]
You can either share your feedback on our [url=https://discord.gg/x5qRfb6gUJ]official Discord[/url] or directly on the Steam Forums! 

[h3]Any bugs to look out for?[/h3]
Because our game is still in Alpha, it unfortunately still has a few bugs here and there. None should greatly hinder your progression, but feel free to check out our list of Known Issues to look out for: https://dotemuhelp.groovehq.com/help/abyssus-technical-support-guide 

Don’t hesitate to report any technical issues you encounter on our official Discord server as well!
Please keep in mind that as the game is still a work in progress, some content may be subject to change based on testing and feedback. Your input during this stage will help us improve the experience and make Abyssus truly unforgettable.

notes.title: FPS Abyssus is allowed to call itself ‘brinepunk’ but you all need to stop this nonsense immediately afterward
notes.notes:
Anyone who is not trying to sell your something will tell you that ‘punk’ is a mostly meaningless term, mainly popularised by Malcolm McLaren and Vivian Westwood so they could sell bondage gear to teenagers. It is, of course, very punk of me to recognise this. However, this hasn’t stopped every other videogame released in the last 74 years trying to coin their own punk subgenre. The latest to do so is ‘brinepunk’ FPS Abyssus, which seems to have mostly arrived at the terms by being ‘a bit Steampunk, but underwater’. Abyssus looks cool, and so with the power vested in me by the Greggs vegan sausage roll I had for lunch today, I hereby declare that this is the last game allowed to do this. Let’s see if it’s making the most of it, at least.
